Access, scaffolding & staging

  • Scaffold & access: Provide scaffolding capable of safely reaching all three stories and roof stacks; scaffolding includes toe boards, debris netting, and safe egress. Scaffold is sized and located to allow continuous work areas and safe removal/reinstallation of railing/lighting. If certain elevations require boom lift access, provide lift pricing as a separate line item or coordinate owner lease.
  • Material staging: Designate staging and material storage areas on site; protect stored materials from weather per manufacturer guidelines.



Removal of existing finish & substrate assessment

  • Controlled removal: Remove unsound/failed stucco and accessory trim in areas identified during field review. Remove to sound attachment and to manufacturer recommended substrate depth; protect adjacent windows, doors, and finishes.
  • Penetration removal: Remove and cap or temporarily protect existing exterior electrical fixtures, cameras, and sensors as necessary for safe work.
  • Substrate inspection: Inspect sheathing, framing, fastener patterns, and existing weather‑resistive barrier behind removed stucco. Identify areas requiring sheathing replacement, structural fastening, or framing repair. Provide written recommendations and quotes for any major repairs beyond localized scope.



Sheathing, weather barrier, and substrate repairs

  • Sheathing replacement: Replace localized damaged sheathing sections with new exterior‑grade sheathing to match existing, fastened per manufacturer and local code requirements. Replace damaged fasteners, plates, or blocking as needed to reestablish continuous substrate.
  • WRB & flashings: Install Tyvek Stucco Wrap or manufacturer‑approved WRB at new framed areas, window/door perimeters, and where existing WRB is compromised. Integrate WRB with through‑wall flashings, sill pan flashings, and head flashings to create a continuous drainage plane.
  • Structural fastening: Where needed, add blocking and fasteners to meet EIFS manufacturer substrate flatness and fastening tolerances for the applied system.



Sloped & level conditions / substrate leveling

  • Flatness tolerances: Mechanically grind, fur out, or furr framing/sheathing to achieve manufacturer required flatness and tolerances (typically within 1/8" over 8' or per product spec). Apply cementitious or polymer modified leveling underlayment where mechanical correction is not practical.
  • Crack stabilization: Rout, clean, and install backer rod and flexible sealant or repair with structural patch to treat active or dormant cracks prior to basecoat installation.
  • Shear/expansion interfaces: Install isolation or movement joints at dissimilar material interfaces, corners, and where long uninterrupted runs exceed manufacturer recommendations.



Moisture & drainage system work

  • Drainage option: For EIFS drainage systems, install drainage mat/mesh and vertical tracks where required by the chosen manufacturer. Provide drip edges, kickout flashings, and weep vents per spec.
  • Flashing terminations: Install manufacturer‑approved termination profiles at window sills, head and jambs, roof terminations, and at any change in plane.   • Insulation board (if specified): Install exterior insulation board (EPS or specified material) with mechanical fasteners and adhesive per system specification, staggered and butted as required to prevent thermal bridging and create continuous insulation plane.
  • Basecoat & mesh: Apply manufacturer specified basecoat to the required thickness, embed fiberglass mesh in basecoat with full lamination, and feather mesh overlaps per spec. Reinforce corners and openings with additional mesh as required.
  • Reinforcement details: Reinforce penetrations, sills, and returns with additional mesh, backings, and termination profiles per manufacturer details.
  • Backer/transition profiles: Install control joints and transition profiles at dissimilar materials and long horizontal runs; use manufacturer approved control joint systems.
  • Finish basecoat preparation: Allow basecoat to cure per manufacturer instructions, then prepare for finish application (light sanding, patching low spots).
  • Finish coat: Apply polymer‑based synthetic finish (smooth steel‑trowel texture) to full elevations in the owner‑selected color. Finish applied by experienced applicators to achieve uniform texture and color consistency; color samples tested and approved by owner prior to full application.



Trim, railings & light fixtures

  • Trim replacement: Remove existing trim to be replaced; install new trim profiles (square look) in materials as specified (fiberglass composite, PVC, or approved wood species) and coordinate terminations with EIFS details. Fasten and seal per manufacturer recommendations to ensure long‑term adhesion.
  • Railing modification: Remove existing railings as required for access. Cut down and re‑weld handrails per dimensional instructions; perform metal fabrication at shop or onsite as agreed. Prime and finish welds with specified corrosion protection; reinstall railings with new fastenings through properly flashed and sleeved openings to avoid compromising WRB.
  • Light relocation: Relocate lights at owner designated positions where indicated. Disconnect/reconnect of fixtures performed per local code by licensed electrician (electrical permit if required). Any new wiring runs, changes to circuits or junctionboxes beyond mechanical relocation are excluded.




Quality control, inspections & testing


  • Moisture testing: If moisture intrusion or elevated moisture is suspected, perform non‑destructive moisture scanning and/or install moisture sensors per manufacturer direction. Additional moisture mitigation is quoted separately if required.
  • Tolerance checks: Verify control joint spacing, flashings, terminations, and color uniformity. Address punchlist items prior to final acceptance.



Cleanup, protection & final closeout

  • Daily cleanup: Maintain a clean and safe work area daily; bag and remove construction debris to approved disposal facilities. Protect driveways and hardscapes from staining using protective coverings.
  • Final punchlist: Conduct owner walk and produce punchlist; schedule corrective work within agreed timeframe. Touch up final finishes and re‑seal terminations as required.
  • Warranties & documentation: Provide workmanship warranty (specify term in contract) and assist owner with manufacturer warranty registration. Provide maintenance recommendations and reseal schedules for joint sealants.



Schedule & sequencing (high level)

  • Mobilization & setup: 1–2 weeks after contract.
  • Removal & substrate repairs: 2–4 weeks (depending on extent of repairs).
  • EIFS installation (board/basecoat/mesh/finish): 3–6 weeks (phased by elevation and weather conditions).
  • Trim, rail, and lighting reinstallation: concurrent with finish work and final punch.

2. GENERAL CONDITIONS & DEMOLITION

  • Protect adjacent finished areas (flooring, walls, cabinetry) with masking and floor protection for the duration of the project.
  • Demolish existing bathroom finishes –  wall surrounds, vanity, toilet, and shower/tub – down to bare studs and subfloor within the work area shown on the plan.
  • Cap and/or relocate existing plumbing and electrical as required 


3. FRAMING

  • Frame the new demising (wet) wall separating Bathroom 1 and Bathroom 2 per plan.
  • Frame new/relocated door openings for each bathroom.
  • Frame any knee walls for both shower enclosures (2 total).
  • Install blocking in walls for vanity/countertop support, mirrors or medicine cabinets, towel bars, future grab bars, and any shower niches.
  • Frame chase/soffit for relocated plumbing vent or exhaust duct routing as needed.

4. PLUMBING
Rough-In:

  • Rough-in supply (hot & cold) and DWV (drain-waste-vent) piping for two (2) full bathrooms, each with one toilet, one vanity sink, and one shower.
  • Extend/relocate piping from the main stack to serve the new fixture layout; run shared wet-wall piping to serve both bathrooms back-to-back.
  • Set shower pans/bases, shower valves, and shower drains (2).
  • Set toilet flanges (2) and vanity sink supply/drain lines (2).
  • Pressure test all new supply and waste lines prior to closing up walls.

Finish:

  • Install finish plumbing fixtures – faucets, shower trim/valves, and toilets – at final phase (fixtures supplied by owner or per allowance, to be confirmed).

5. ELECTRICAL

  • Rough-in and install lighting circuits for both bathrooms, including vanity light fixtures (2) and general/overhead lighting.
  • Install shower-rated recessed light where applicable (2).
  • Install GFCI-protected receptacles at each vanity (2), per code.
  • Install exhaust fan circuits and vent fans for each bathroom (2), ducted to the exterior per code.
  • Install switches for lighting and exhaust fans at each bathroom entry.
  • Confirm main panel capacity for added circuits/loads; add or relocate circuits as needed.
  • Final trim: switch plates, receptacle covers, light fixtures, and fan grilles (2 each).

MASTER BEDROOM

  • Standard exterior/interior wall framing around the room
  • Shared wall with Master Bath has a built-in fireplace — needs a framed fireplace chase/cavity
  • Two pocket door openings in that same wall: one into the Master Bath toilet room, one into the Master Closet — pocket doors need a double-stud rough opening with room inside the wall for the door to slide into (can't use a standard 2x4 wall for these, needs a wider pocket door frame kit)

MASTER BATH — TOILET ROOM (the small enclosed WC)

  • Frame a fully separate small room in the corner of the Master Bath, walled off on all sides
  • One pocket door (2'-8") for privacy
  • Small linen shelf nook next to it — needs blocking for shelves

MASTER BATH — main area 

  • Long dual vanity wall (96"): plumbing wall behind it for the two sinks, plus backing for the cabinet and mirrors
  • 2x6 wall recommended anywhere pipes run (vanity wall, shower wall)

MASTER CLOSET

  • Frame walls separating it from the Master Bath (pocket door connects them) and from the hallway/Bath 2 area below it
  • Blocking in the walls for the built-in shelf-and-rod system (marked "R&S" on plan)

BATH 2 (serves Bedroom 2)

  • Tub + toilet alcove framed together on one wall
  • Separate vanity wall (44") with plumbing behind it
    • Entry door from hallway (2'-8"), pocket door toward Bedroom 2 side
  • Linen shelf nook (R&S)

BATH 1 (serves Bedroom 1, near hallway)

  • Fully enclosed shower stall — its own small framed room with a door swing (not pocket)
  • Toilet sits in the same room as the shower, so just the one enclosure
  • Small linen niche built into the wall (recessed shelf — frame it shallower than a normal wall, usually between studs of a 2x6 wall)

HALLWAY

  • Central spine wall with two pocket doors branching off to Bath 2 and Bedroom areas
  • Standard framing otherwise, just the connector between all the bedrooms/baths and the main living area

BEDROOM 1 & BEDROOM 2

  • Standard 2x4 walls
  • Closets get 5'-0" sliding doors and blocking for rod-and-shelf

COVERED ENTRY

  • Just the exterior wall opening for the 3'-0" front door — no interior framing needed here, it's outdoor space



    DRYWALL (interior)

    • Hang drywall on all interior walls and ceilings
    • 5/8" fire-rated drywall on garage walls/ceiling shared with house
    • Tape, mud, and finish all walls/ceilings
    • Standard knockdown texture (confirm if owner wants smooth instead)
    • NOT included: insulation, garage finish beyond code minimum

    PAINT — Interior

    • Patch, caulk, and prep all walls
    • Prime all new drywall
    • 2 coats paint on walls, 2 coats on ceilings
    • Paint/stain doors, trim, baseboards
    • Includes closets, pantry, laundry
    • Garage interior paint only if requested

    PAINT — Exterior

    • Pressure wash and prep stucco
    • Prime stucco
    • 2 coats exterior paint on all stucco walls
    • Paint trim, fascia, garage door, entry door
    • Paint patio/entry ceilings

    • • NOT included: stucco application itself, roofing, gutters
